scope: exact_ldexp is exact exponent adjustment only for supported finite-normal binary64 intermediates and signed zero; it is not a full-domain IEEE754 ldexp replacement. Unsupported inputs set sticky fault bit1 and return0.

input_contract.samples: IEEE float32 finite within [-1,1], including signed zero and float subnormals
input_contract.window: Unmodified original C++ symmetric Hann2048, with exact exported binary64 constants
input_contract.gain: original LogMMSE gain clamped to binary64 [.1,1]

analytical_bounds.unpacked_fft_bound_scope: Conservative signed48 output bound, stronger real vendor valid44bit bound is not required. Exact integer/2^31 unpacking.
analytical_bounds.explanation: Every nonzero float32 converts exactly to a normal double. Multiplication by nonzero Hann keeps magnitude >2^-168. frexp-style normalization uses the frame maximum exponent and cannot exceed .5. Signed48 FFT words unpack exactly; restoration and gain [.1,1] establish second normalization bounds. Inverse restoration adds second_exp-9. Thus no helper input or target can be double subnormal/nonfinite in this supported domain. Zero takes its explicit signed-zero branch. Quantization may intentionally round tiny normalized values to integer0, as the reference vendor fixed FFT does.

boundary_tests.level: Csim with real Xilinx bitacc FFT Cmodel; not yet actual RTL boundary-stream evidence
boundary_tests.quantizer: ties-to-even at selected Q31 integer boundaries and both IEEE64 nextafter neighbors, positive and negative, independently checked with nearbyint(ldexp(x,31))
boundary_tests.note: These tests corroborate the stated domain bounds; sampled tests are not described as an all-IEEE formal proof.
boundary_tests.reuse_scope: Unchanged exact_ldexp/quantize helper source and original constants; R5 differs only HLS internal RAM/ROM port pragmas. Boundary helper tests were run on R4 code, not claimed as R5 actual RTL.

continued_fraction: iteration_bounds.json gives cap55 analytical denominator/rounding bounds and1250000-point corroboration.

whole_vendor_kernel_conversion_semantics.scope: The bounds above prove exact_ldexp helper supported normal-double exponent adjustment and safe numeric magnitudes, not complete all-IEEE behavior of every vendor operator.
whole_vendor_kernel_conversion_semantics.float32_subnormal_inputs_or_outputs: Actual selected FPEXT and FPTRUNC IP flush abs<2^-126 to signedzero. Normal real-recording equivalence is independently tested; arbitrary subnormal CPU bit equivalence is not claimed.
